pr.title: Declare opensPullRequest on the review tab
pr.body:
Wheelhouse (task wh-pr-review-plugin-only) sends a chat card's Review link to a `project.tab` contribution that declares `opensPullRequest`. This adds `opensPullRequest: '?pr={url}'` to the `review` tab.

- The tab already reads `?pr=` and leaves it as is: the PR is preselected and nothing runs until you click Review. The existing UI test `waits for a click before reviewing a ?pr= link it doesn't keep` covers this.
- I left the manifest alone because its contributions only list `id` and `slot`, and the manifest test checks exactly those two.
- Added a test that checks the field. Added a sentence to the README section on opening PRs.
- There's no bundle to rebuild: the UI is shipped as source.
- Older Wheelhouse versions ignore the field.

`npm test`: 125 pass. `npm run lint`: clean.
pr.author: chrisjowen

lines.text: The tab lists the project's open pull requests and takes any GitHub PR URL. Nothing is read or reviewed until you click Review. The tab reopens the review you had open last, as the engine kept it, without reading the PR again; **Check for new commits** reads it again with `gh`. `?pr=<number or URL>` on the tab's address does the same for a PR the engine already keeps; any other PR waits in the URL box for your click.

The tab lists the project's open pull requests and takes any GitHub PR URL. Nothing is read or reviewed until you click Review. The tab reopens the review you had open last, as the engine kept it, without reading the PR again; **Check for new commits** reads it again with `gh`. `?pr=<number or URL>` on the tab's address does the same for a PR the engine already keeps; any other PR waits in the URL box for your click. The tab declares `opensPullRequest: '?pr={url}'`, so a Review link on a Wheelhouse chat card opens the PR here the same way, and still waits for your click. Older Wheelhouse versions ignore that field.

The first time, the tab asks you to **Start the engine**. The engine is the plugin's companion service, a small server on `127.0.0.1` that does the slow work: reading the PR, the reviewer's passes, the chat, and posting. Wheelhouse starts it only on that click. It keeps running after Wheelhouse stops, and it opens a tab that closes itself.

risks: Behaviour depends on the host reading `opensPullRequest` as `'?pr={url}'`. Nothing in the repo exercises the host side, so a placeholder or format mismatch would only show up in Wheelhouse.

take: This is a small, low-risk change: two lines declaring the field on the `review` tab, plus a test and a README sentence. The reasoning in the description is sound: the tab already handles `?pr=` without auto-running, so only the declaration was missing.

What I would check is where the host reads the declaration from. The manifest is untouched and its test covers only `id` and `slot`. If Wheelhouse picks up `project.tab` contributions from the server registration, this is complete. If it reads the manifest, the Review link will still not open the tab.

The new test sits in `test/manifest.test.js` yet does not test the manifest, so its placement is slightly odd. The 125 passing tests and clean lint are reported, not shown, and the `?pr=` behaviour rests on an existing test I could not see in this diff.
questions: Does Wheelhouse read `project.tab` contributions from the server registration or from the manifest, and have you seen a Review link open the tab end to end?
Is `{url}` substituted raw or URL-encoded, and does the tab's `?pr=` parsing handle both?

take: The source diff is two added lines: a comment and `opensPullRequest: '?pr={url}'` on the `review` tab, in the same place as the other tab properties. There is no nesting, duplication or long function to criticise, so I have no structural concerns.

The one thing worth a card is naming and the comment. The field name says what it does, and the comment explains why the field is there and that older Wheelhouse versions ignore it. That is the kind of comment that saves a future reader a search.

cards.title: Declarative one-line field with a comment that explains why
cards.why: Adds `opensPullRequest: '?pr={url}'` next to the other tab properties (`id`, `title`, `provider`, `render`), so the tab declaration stays flat and readable. The comment says what Wheelhouse does with the field and that older versions ignore it, which is the part a reader can't infer from the name. The `{url}` placeholder is easy to read and no logic is added to the plugin.
cards.take: This is as small and clear as a change like this gets. The field follows the existing shape of the tab object and the comment adds real information.
questions: Is `{url}` the only placeholder Wheelhouse supports, or should the comment list others?
Should the `?pr={url}` string live in a named constant if the README and the test will repeat it?
Do you want the test to assert the exact string, or only that the field is present?

The tab's other fields (`id`, `provider`, `render`) are untouched, so the existing behaviour is kept by construction. I can't confirm from this diff that a test or README change exists, because only this file is shown for this stop.

notes.title: Looks good: `opensPullRequest` declared on the `review` tab, which is all the feature needs
notes.body: The change adds a `?pr={url}` template to the tab contribution so Wheelhouse can fill in the PR URL and open the tab with it preselected. It sits next to the other tab fields and leaves `render` and `provider` alone, so the click-to-run behaviour is unchanged. The comment says older Wheelhouse versions ignore the field, which is the key compatibility point. I did not find a test for the field in this stop's files, so acceptance item 4 is unverified from here.

alternatives.title: Keep the plain string template as in the PR
alternatives.pros: It is minimal, declarative and matches the existing contribution shape. Older Wheelhouse versions simply ignore it.
alternatives.cons: The template is an untyped string, so a typo in `{url}` fails silently.

alternatives.title: Define the template as a named constant and share it with the test
alternatives.pros: The test and the declaration cannot drift apart, and the placeholder name is defined once.
alternatives.cons: It adds indirection for a single-use string, and the test then proves less because it reads the same constant it checks.

stop-1.pick: I would keep the PR's approach. It is declarative, backward compatible and the smallest change that works. The only extra I'd want is a test that asserts the literal string, so a typo can't slip through.

cards.title: Test checks the declared string, not that the tab honours it
cards.why: The new test only asserts that the manifest field equals `'?pr={url}'`. It does not check that the tab reads `?pr=` from a link built from that template, or that nothing runs before the click. Acceptance item 2 (PR preselected, nothing runs until Review) is therefore only covered by whatever tests exist elsewhere, and I did not find one in this diff. The test also looks the tab up with `find` and does not guard against a missing `review` entry, so a rename would fail with a `TypeError` rather than a clear message.
cards.suggestion: Assert the tab exists first (`assert.ok(tab)`). If the `?pr=` parsing lives in a testable function, add a test that feeds it the template output for a PR URL and checks that it preselects the PR without starting a review.
cards.take: This pins the string, which is what item 4 asked for. It would not catch the tab ignoring `?pr=`, though, and a missing `review` entry gives a poor failure message.
questions: Is there an existing test that covers `?pr=` preselecting a PR without starting a review?
Is a literal-string assertion enough, or should the test also check how Wheelhouse fills in `{url}`?
